title: Coniveau edge and its normalized flag components
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and let $S$ be a Noetherian excellent normal strictly henselian local scheme of dimension $d\geq2$, with closed point $s$ and $\ell$ invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Put $U=S\setminus\{s\}$ and $U^p=\{y\in U:\dim\mathcal O_{S,y}=p\}$. Use ordinary etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], cohomology with supports [def-pur-etale-derived-supported-sections], and cohomological spectral sequences [def-sp-spectral-sequence], costalks $C_y$, and the normalized immediate transitions and twists of [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. There is a convergent cohomological coniveau spectral sequence
$$E_1^{p,q}=\bigoplus_{y\in U^p}H^{p+q}_{\{y\}}(\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O^h_{S,y},\Lambda(d))\Longrightarrow H^{p+q}(U,\Lambda(d)).$$
Here $\mathcal O^h_{S,y}$ is the henselization (a henselian local ring universal among henselian local rings receiving a local map from $\mathcal O_{S,y}$), and local supported cohomology identifies with $R\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y),C_y\Lambda(d))$. Suppose for every $y\in U^p$ the sheaves $\mathcal H^j(C_y\Lambda(p))$ vanish for $j>2p$, and an isomorphism $\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^{2p}(C_y\Lambda(p))$, $1\mapsto e_y$, is specified on the residue-field etale site [def-weil-residue-field]. Suppose also that every $\Lambda$-module etale sheaf on $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(y)$ has no cohomology in degrees greater than $d-p$. Then $E_1^{p,q}=0$ for $q>d$ or $p\notin[0,d-1]$, and
$$E_1^{p,d}\cong\bigoplus_{y\in U^p}H^{d-p}(\kappa(y),\Lambda(d-p)).$$
The canonical edge, followed by the localization boundary, gives an isomorphism
$$\operatorname{coker}(E_1^{d-2,d}\xrightarrow{d_1}E_1^{d-1,d})\xrightarrow{\sim}H^{2d}_s(S,\Lambda(d)).$$
For $y\in U^{d-1}$ the normalized valuation residue is an isomorphism $\rho_y:H^1(\kappa(y),\Lambda(1))\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda$: normalize the reduced closure of $y$ in $S$, take the tame residue of its strictly henselian trait, and multiply by the purely inseparable degree $a_y$ of its closed point over $s$. Thus $\rho_y=a_y\operatorname{res}_y$; this is the coefficient dual to the inverse-degree normalization of the transition. Under the above identification, there is a sign $\epsilon\in\{1,-1\}$, depending only on the sign conventions of the localization boundary, of the residue and of the trait transition (not on $S$, $y$ or $b$), such that the map from this $y$-summand to $H^{2d}_s(S,\Lambda(d))$ is
$$b\longmapsto\epsilon\,\rho_y(b)\operatorname{sp}_{\bar y,\bar s}(e_{\bar y}),$$
where the transition is twisted by $d-1$ and $e_{\bar y}$ is the geometric fibre of $e_y$. In particular the image of this summand is $\Lambda\operatorname{sp}_{\bar y,\bar s}(e_{\bar y})$.

source.place: Expose XVII, proof of Lemma 3.6.2, printed pp. 278–279: coniveau sequence, top-edge calculation, and the normalized component identification after the displayed sum of H^1(y,Lambda(1)). The same calculation applies for d=2 once the transition theorem is supplied independently

proof.text: A normal local ring is a domain by [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Excellence supplies catenarity [def-exc-excellent-ring]. A saturated chain from the generic point to a point $y$ has length $\dim\mathcal O_{S,y}$; concatenating with a saturated chain from $y$ to $s$ gives length $d$. Consequently this codimension takes values $0,\ldots,d-1$ on $U$ and increases by one at immediate specializations. Apply [lem-per-codimension-support-filtration] to $X=U$, $N=d-1$, $K=\Lambda(d)$. Apply [thm-sp-spectral-object-yields] to its bounded filtered complex. The graded-complex identification gives exactly the asserted $E_1$ page, henselian local-term description, abutment, and differential bidegree $(r,1-r)$. Finite filtration gives convergence without a limiting assumption.

source.place: XVII, proof of Lemma 3.6.2, printed pp. 278–279

proof.text: For $y\in U^p$ put $K_y=C_y\Lambda(d)$. The rank-one twist comparisons [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] identify $K_y=C_y\Lambda(p)(d-p)$: after etale trivialization of the twist this is the identity for the supported kernel defining $C_y$, hence also for its derived functor. In particular $\mathcal H^jK_y=0$ for $j>2p$ and $\mathcal H^{2p}K_y=\Lambda(d-p)$ via the specified $e_y$. The residue-field module sheaf category is Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-grothendieck-abelian]. Apply [thm-sp-truncation-e2] to its global-sections functor and $K_y$. Its page is $H^a(\kappa(y),\mathcal H^bK_y)$, zero unless $0\leq a\leq d-p$ and $b\leq2p$. Thus total degrees above $d+p$ vanish. In total degree $d+p$ only $(a,b)=(d-p,2p)$ survives; all incoming terms have $b>2p$ and all outgoing terms have $a>d-p$. The finite abutment filtration therefore canonically identifies $H^{d+p}(\kappa(y),K_y)$ with $H^{d-p}(\kappa(y),\Lambda(d-p))$. Taking the direct sums proves the asserted vanishing and top row.

source.place: XVII, proof of Lemma 3.6.2, printed pp. 278–279

proof.text: On total degree $2d-1$ the rectangle $0\leq p\leq d-1$, $q\leq d$ has just the corner $(d-1,d)$. No differential leaves it. For $r\geq2$ a differential entering it would come from $(d-1-r,d+r-1)$, which is zero. Hence $E_\infty^{d-1,d}=E_2^{d-1,d}=\operatorname{coker}(E_1^{d-2,d}\to E_1^{d-1,d})$. The finite filtration has a single nonzero graded term in this total degree, so the corner edge is an isomorphism onto $H^{2d-1}(U,\Lambda(d))$. This argument also covers $d=2$, where the displayed incoming $d_1$ starts in column zero.

source.place: XVII, proof of Lemma 3.6.2, printed pp. 278–279

proof.text: The localization triangle [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle], followed by derived global sections, gives the exact segment $H^{2d-1}(S,\Lambda(d))\to H^{2d-1}(U,\Lambda(d))\to H_s^{2d}(S,\Lambda(d))\to H^{2d}(S,\Lambda(d))$. Both outside terms vanish by [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-etale-acyclic], applied to the underlying abelian sheaf of $\Lambda(d)$: global sections of $\Lambda$-module sheaves are computed on underlying abelian sheaves, and a short exact sequence of module sheaves is exact as abelian sheaves, so global sections are exact on $\Lambda$-module sheaves and their higher derived functors vanish; here $2d-1>0$. The middle boundary is therefore an isomorphism. Composing with Step 3 proves the asserted cokernel isomorphism.

source.place: XVII, proof of Lemma 3.6.2, printed pp. 278–279

proof.text: Fix $y\in U^{d-1}$. The reduced closure $Z$ of $y$ in $S$ is one-dimensional by the saturated-chain calculation of Step 1, and is local with closed point $s$. Fix compatible geometric lifts. The normalization and costalk identifications of [lem-per-prime-power-costalk-reduction] give a strictly henselian trait $\nu:V\to Z$ with generic field $\kappa(y)$, a finite purely inseparable closed residue extension of degree $a_y\in\Lambda^\times$, and an equivalence of etale categories. Put $L=\nu^*i^!\Lambda(d)$, $i:Z\hookrightarrow S$. Its geometric generic stalk is $C_{\bar y}\Lambda(d)$ and its supported complex is $C_{\bar s}\Lambda(d)$. The last-column map followed by the boundary of Step 4 is the boundary $H^{2d-1}(\kappa(y),L_\eta)\to H^{2d}_{s_V}(V,L)$: this is precisely the boundary compatibility in [lem-per-codimension-support-filtration], followed by the normalization equivalence. The supported-composition identifications are [lem-per-prime-power-supported-calculus]. No fundamental class at $s$ or chain-independence theorem is used.

source.place: XVII, proof of Lemma 3.6.2, printed pp. 278–279

proof.text: On $V$, apply [lem-per-prime-power-trait-residue-model] to the constant sheaf $\Lambda(1)$; it is constant because the residue field is separably closed and $\ell$ is invertible, so all $\ell^n$-th roots of unity are sections of $V$. Its supported complex has identity first differential and zero second differential, hence $H^2_{s_V}(V,\Lambda(1))=\operatorname{Hom}_A(I,\Lambda(1))$. By [lem-per-prime-power-trait-generic-boundary-model], part (b), with acyclicity [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-etale-acyclic] of the closed-stalk column, the localization boundary of [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] is an isomorphism $H^1(\kappa(y),\Lambda(1))\to H^2_{s_V}(V,\Lambda(1))$, sending the class of $f_c$ in the generic model to $\epsilon_0f_c$. Evaluation at $1-\sigma$ is an isomorphism because multiplication by $1-\sigma$ identifies $A$ with $I$. Untwisting by the image $\zeta_\sigma$ of $\sigma$ in $G/\ell^n=\mu_{\ell^n}$ defines $\operatorname{res}_y:H^1(\kappa(y),\Lambda(1))\simeq\Lambda$; replacing $\sigma$ by $\sigma^\alpha$ multiplies both the value at $1-\sigma$ and $\zeta_\sigma$ by $\alpha$ (trivial action), so $\operatorname{res}_y$ is independent of $\sigma$. This is the valuation residue up to sign: by [lem-per-trait-tame-algebra] the tame quotient is the action on roots of a uniformizer $\pi$, so the Kummer cocycle of $\pi$ is $c(\sigma)=\zeta_\sigma$, and [lem-per-augmentation-cocycle-comparison] gives $f_c(1-\sigma)=-\zeta_\sigma$, whence $\operatorname{res}_y(\kappa(\pi))=-\epsilon_0$. Multiplication by the unit $a_y$ proves that the corrected $\rho_y=a_y\operatorname{res}_y$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: XVII section 1.3 (tame augmentation resolution) and Lemma 3.6.2, p. 279

proof.text: Compute the boundary of Step 5 using the same trait resolution. By [lem-per-prime-power-trait-generic-boundary-model], applied to a bounded below complex representing $L$, $R\Gamma(\kappa(y),L_\eta)$ is the generic model $C(L)$ and the boundary sends the class of a cocycle $(0,x)$ of $C(L)$, $x\in\operatorname{Hom}_A(I,L^{2d-2}_{\bar\eta}{}^S)$, to $\epsilon_0x$ in the degree-two column of the supported total complex $F(L)$ of [lem-per-prime-power-trait-residue-model]. By the vanishing of generic cohomology sheaves above $2d-2$ (Step 2) every class of degree $2d-1$ has such a representative. Write a class as $b\,e_y$ by the top truncation in Step 2. For its character $\chi$, that component evaluates at $1-\sigma$ to $\chi(\sigma)e_{\bar y}$. In the cochain formula for $\operatorname{sp}_V$, averaging fixes the invariant class $e_{\bar y}$, and inverse evaluation at $1-\sigma$ gives the same component. Therefore the boundary class is $\epsilon\operatorname{res}_y(b)\operatorname{sp}_V(e_{\bar y})$, with the indicated twist. This remains true if a cocycle representing $e_y$ is changed by a coboundary: both constructions are cochain maps with the same evaluation component and hence give equal cohomology classes. The top-truncation identification uses no other generic cohomology term, by the degree calculation in Step 2. The only possible signs are $\epsilon_0$ of the boundary model and the sign of the augmentation comparison; the shift $m=2d-2$ is even, so it contributes no sign varying with $d$. Thus $\epsilon$ depends only on the three fixed conventions.

source.place: XVII section 1.3 (explicit supported complex and transition) and Lemma 3.6.2, last paragraph

proof.text: By [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex], the immediate transition on $S$ is $\operatorname{sp}_{\bar y,\bar s}=a_y^{-1}\operatorname{sp}_V$, with the source twisted by $d-1$. Substitution into Step 7 gives $\epsilon a_y\operatorname{res}_y(b)\operatorname{sp}_{\bar y,\bar s}(e_{\bar y})=\epsilon\rho_y(b)\operatorname{sp}_{\bar y,\bar s}(e_{\bar y})$. Since $\rho_y$ is onto and $\epsilon$ is a unit, its image is exactly $\Lambda\operatorname{sp}_{\bar y,\bar s}(e_{\bar y})$. This last subgroup is unaffected by the correction from inverse degree to degree in the coefficient.

No SGA source is cited. STATEMENT CORRECTION ACCEPTED: def-per-potential-dualizing-complex (= ILO Def 1.3.1) sets sp_S = a^{-1}·sp_V. The equivalence ν^* carries the localization boundary on Z to the one on V with no factor, so the component is ±a·res(b)·sp_S(e). The old ρ = a^{-1}·res was off by a² (worker's example: k[[u,v]], v²−tu², char 2, Λ=F_7). ILO states only the image, which is unchanged, and the sole citer lem-per-normal-top-residue-class (Steps 7–9) uses only the image and surjectivity. STEPS: Step 1 is right: in a catenary local domain, concatenating saturated chains gives ht p + dim A/p = d, so c rises by one at immediate specializations; filtered spectral sequence. Step 2 is right: truncation E2 with a ≤ d−p, b ≤ 2p leaves only the corner (d−p, 2p). Step 3 is right: corner (d−1, d), no differentials for r ≥ 2, F^d = 0, d = 2 fine. Step 4 is right; I added the sentence that Λ-module Γ is exact on the strictly henselian S. Step 5 is right: Z = {y, s} meets the child's boundary clause exactly; costalk-reduction gives V, a_y and the ν^* equivalence. Step 8 is right. FAULT (C3/D5, Steps 6–7): both steps computed the boundary of a generic cocycle as its degree-two Hom_A(I,−) component, but lem-per-prime-power-trait-residue-model states only F ≅ RΓ_s. It gives no model of RΓ(η) and none of the boundary, and lem-per-trait-gysin-residue has that model only inside its proof. It says (a) C(K) = Tot[K^S → Hom_A(I,K^S)] ≅ RΓ(η,K), with the degree-one comparison of lem-per-augmentation-cocycle-comparison; (b) 0 → C[−1] → F → K_s → 0 is the localization triangle, up to a convention sign ε_0. Step 6 is rewritten to cite it, plus lem-per-trait-tame-algebra (Kummer cocycle of π is ζ_σ, so res(κ(π)) = ±1) and the σ-independence check. Step 7 now cites it and justifies the (0,x) representative by top-degree vanishing. proof_deps updated; the statement is unchanged.
